Zeremonie.et: From Middle High German cerimōnie, from Medieval Latin ceremonia, from classical caeremōnia. At first only in ecclesiastical context; broader use since ca. 1600 after French cérémonie, which also caused the now predominant final stress.

s: cereal; a type of grass cultivated for its edible grains
Zerealie.et: Borrowed from Latin Cerealis. The sense ‘breakfast cereal’ is a semantic loan from English cereal.

Zeremonienmeister.et: From Zeremonie + -n- + Meister. The word preserves an older stress pattern of the first component.

zeremoniell.et: By surface analysis, Zeremonie + -ell. Borrowed from French cérémoniel.
